report_name: Russian APT BlueDelta Targets European Governments with HOOKEDGE Backdoor

threat_actors.name: BlueDelta
threat_actors.description: A Russian GRU-linked threat group that conducted a targeted espionage campaign against European government and diplomatic entities using the HOOKEDGE backdoor. The campaign was active from late 2025 to early 2026.
threat_actors.goals: Espionage against NATO members and European government entities to steal diplomatic and government documents.

attack_patterns.name: Spearphishing Attachment
attack_patterns.description: The attack chain began with spear-phishing emails containing malicious macro-enabled Microsoft Word documents with diplomatic-themed lures.

attack_patterns.name: Visual Basic
attack_patterns.description: Malicious Visual Basic for Applications (VBA) macros within the Word document were used to drop and execute the HOOKEDGE backdoor script.

attack_patterns.name: Windows Command Shell
attack_patterns.description: The HOOKEDGE backdoor is a Windows batch script that is executed by the command shell.

attack_patterns.name: Scheduled Task
attack_patterns.description: The HOOKEDGE backdoor established persistence by creating a scheduled task that ran every 30 minutes.

attack_patterns.name: Obfuscated Files or Information
attack_patterns.description: The malicious macros within the Word document were obfuscated to evade detection.

attack_patterns.name: Deobfuscate/Decode Files or Information
attack_patterns.description: The malicious macro decodes and drops the HOOKEDGE batch script onto the victim's system.

attack_patterns.name: Web Protocols
attack_patterns.description: The HOOKEDGE backdoor used HTTP POST requests for command and control communications with the webhook.site service.

attack_patterns.name: Remote Access Software
attack_patterns.description: The legitimate web service 'webhook.site' was abused for command and control functions, making the malicious traffic difficult to distinguish from benign developer activity.

attack_patterns.name: Ingress Tool Transfer
attack_patterns.description: The HOOKEDGE backdoor downloaded commands from an attacker-controlled URL hosted on the webhook.site service.

malware.name: HOOKEDGE
malware.description: A lightweight backdoor written as a Windows batch script. It establishes C2 communication using the webhook.site service, downloads and executes commands, and exfiltrates the results.

tools.name: Microsoft Edge
tools.description: Used in headless mode (`--headless`) by the HOOKEDGE backdoor to perform C2 communications with webhook.site, helping to blend in with normal user activity.

tools.name: schtasks
tools.description: Used by the HOOKEDGE backdoor to create a scheduled task for persistence, ensuring the malware runs every 30 minutes.

campaigns.name: BlueDelta HOOKEDGE Campaign 2025-2026
campaigns.description: An espionage campaign by BlueDelta (APT28) from late 2025 to early 2026, targeting European government and diplomatic organizations with the HOOKEDGE backdoor, which used webhook.site for C2.
campaigns.objective: Espionage against European government and diplomatic entities.

identities.name: Government and diplomatic organizations in Romania
identities.description: Targeted by the BlueDelta espionage campaign using the HOOKEDGE backdoor.

identities.name: Government and diplomatic organizations in Spain
identities.description: Targeted by the BlueDelta espionage campaign using the HOOKEDGE backdoor.

identities.name: Government and diplomatic organizations in Türkiye
identities.description: Targeted by the BlueDelta espionage campaign using the HOOKEDGE backdoor.

identities.name: Spain's Ministry of the Presidency
identities.description: Impersonated in a malicious document lure, indicating it was a target of the BlueDelta campaign.

infrastructure.name: webhook.site C2 Service
infrastructure.description: The legitimate developer service 'webhook.site' was abused for C2 communications. HOOKEDGE used unique URLs on this service to fetch commands and exfiltrate data via HTTP POST requests.

indicators.name: HOOKEDGE C2 Communication to webhook.site
indicators.x_netsecio_sigma_rule:
title: HOOKEDGE C2 Communication via webhook.site
id: 4a7b1c8d-e9f0-4a1b-8c2d-3e4f5a6b7c8d
status: experimental
description: Detects network connections to webhook.site, which is abused by the HOOKEDGE backdoor for C2. This may cause false positives in environments with developers using this service.
references:
  - https://securityaffairs.com/197996/apt/russian-apt-bluedelta-uses-hookedge-to-target-defense-and-diplomatic-organizations.html
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-29
tags:
  - attack.t1071.001
  - attack.t1219
  - attack.command_and_control
level: medium
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate use of webhook.site by developers.
logsource:
  category: proxy
detection:
  selection:
    cs-host: 'webhook.site'
  filter_dev:
    c-user-agent|contains:
      - 'Postman'
      - 'curl'
    # Add other legitimate developer tool user agents
  condition: selection and not filter_dev
indicators.description: Detects network traffic to webhook.site, a legitimate service abused by the HOOKEDGE backdoor for command and control. Legitimate developer traffic may cause false positives.

indicators.name: Suspicious Headless Browser Execution for C2
indicators.pattern:
title: Suspicious Headless Browser Execution for C2
id: f8a7b6c5-d4e3-4f2a-1b0c-9d8e7f6a5b4c
status: experimental
description: Detects Microsoft Edge or Google Chrome running in headless mode, a TTP used by the HOOKEDGE backdoor to perform C2 communications while blending in with normal activity.
references:
  - https://securityaffairs.com/197996/apt/russian-apt-bluedelta-uses-hookedge-to-target-defense-and-diplomatic-organizations.html
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-29
tags:
  - attack.t1071.001
  - attack.command_and_control
level: high
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate automated testing or web scraping scripts.
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\msedge.exe'
      - '\chrome.exe'
    CommandLine|contains: '--headless'
  filter_legit_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      # Add legitimate parent processes for automated testing tools if necessary
      - '\wdagtool.exe'
  condition: selection and not filter_legit_parent
indicators.description: Detects the execution of Microsoft Edge or Google Chrome with the '--headless' flag, which is highly anomalous for user activity and was used by HOOKEDGE for C2.

indicators.name: HOOKEDGE Persistence via Scheduled Task
indicators.pattern:
title: HOOKEDGE Persistence via Scheduled Task
id: 1a2b3c4d-5e6f-4a7b-8c9d-0e1f2a3b4c5d
status: experimental
description: Detects the creation of a scheduled task executing a batch script, which is the persistence mechanism used by the HOOKEDGE backdoor.
references:
  - https://securityaffairs.com/197996/apt/russian-apt-bluedelta-uses-hookedge-to-target-defense-and-diplomatic-organizations.html
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-29
tags:
  - attack.t1053.005
  - attack.persistence
level: medium
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate administrative scripts creating scheduled tasks.
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\schtasks.exe'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - '/create'
      - '.bat'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the creation of a scheduled task that executes a batch file, a technique used by HOOKEDGE for persistence.
